discovery_basis: Only the supplied brief and listed web sources; exact plan unreleased at time of discovery.

sources.title: Changes in the macro and nano-structure of paper during moisture cycling
sources.version_or_release: Original research; published online 2023-12-20; Cellulose 31, 2743–2764 (2024); DOI 10.1007/s10570-023-05626-6.
sources.locator: Abstract; Background; Methods lines 109–127; Results lines 156–171.
sources.observed_operation: Laboratory pulp sheets of differing furnish/processing and restrained/free drying were measured before/after four 50→20→90→50% RH cycles at 23°C, held at least 24 h per RH step; ≥5 strain specimens per paper.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reported test conditions and measured material behavior only; no collection storage default or universal paper behavior. Initial-cycle response and irreversible change differed with sheet preparation/restraint.
sources.applicability: Primary evidence for paper hygroexpansion/cycling and the need to control sheet identity and drying restraint. Laboratory pulp sheets are not these printed, adhesive-backed labels; the study cycle is not a recommended case test envelope.
sources.evidence_used: Conditional mechanism and choice of separate dimensional endpoint; proposed controls and limitations.

sources.title: Long term curl of printing paper due to ink solvent migration
sources.version_or_release: Published article version; Materials & Design 237 (2024), article 112593; DOI 10.1016/j.matdes.2023.112593.
sources.locator: PDF pp. 4–9, especially §1.3.2–1.4, §2.1–2.2; pp. 5–6 lines 284–328 and pp. 7–9 lines 393–438 in indexed full text.
sources.observed_operation: Primary laboratory study applied a 60 wt% glycerol/water model ink to two office paper grades, monitored curl and glycerol migration over a one-week storage interval, and examined the role of paper and print/drying process.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Mechanism is conditional on tested paper and water-based model ink; the study is not a general default for every printer technology or label.
sources.applicability: Supports asking about ink/toner/ribbon, stock, one-sided wetting and drying only if actual printing process matches. Does not establish the case's process or sleeve-label attachment behavior.
sources.evidence_used: Conditional print-related curl hypothesis and explicit one-week evidence scope.

sources.title: RXC Specification for Pressure Sensitive Adhesive Labels for Laser Printing
sources.version_or_release: October 2015 specification; labels for archival housings/storage furniture; PDF says new specification as of 2015.
sources.locator: PDF pp. 1–3, §§ I–II, bond strength, print/readability, workmanship and QC table; indexed lines 1–16, 45–75, 82–101.
sources.observed_operation: Specifies paper face stock with acrylic PSA for the stated laser application; calls for a 90° peel method modified from ASTM D2860/D2860M-04 and a 1×2.5 in coupon supporting 200 g for 10 minutes; separately specifies legibility/scanner and flatness/ooze; lot-level QA.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies to labels on paper/board/plastic/metal housings and metal furniture; explicitly not suitable for direct application to documents or records. Printer/toner, dimensions and label configuration are specified by procurement.
sources.applicability: A dated institutional procurement specification and test-design lead, not a collection-wide conservation standard or evidence that its permanent adhesive is safe/reversible on a particular sleeve.
sources.evidence_used: System-level records request, test endpoints and limitations; no NARA product recommended.

sources.title: RXC Specification for Pressure Sensitive Adhesive Labels for Thermal Transfer Printers
sources.version_or_release: October 2015 revision; revision note says revised from May 2013, previously reformatted September 2010.
sources.locator: PDF pp. 1–3, §§ I–II and QC table; indexed lines 1–18, 26–51, 67–81.
sources.observed_operation: Specifies polyester or polypropylene film face stock bearing acrylic PSA, hard-resin thermal transfer ribbon, no wax or wax/resin ribbon; notes polypropylene preferred for curved substrate; includes a 90° peel coupon test and separate print/flatness checks.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies to housing/furniture labels for the stated thermal transfer configuration; exact printer/ribbon and dimensions are procurement-selected. Not a default for unidentified materials or handwritten annotations.
sources.applicability: Useful comparison for process/material compatibility and version history, but neither a performance guarantee for this sleeve nor proof of archival safety.
sources.evidence_used: Implementation-history fields and conditional test matrix; no stock or adhesive recommendation.

sources.title: Incorrect relative humidity
sources.creators: Canadian Conservation Institute, Government of Canada
sources.version_or_release: Current online guidance; no dated edition/version displayed on the accessed page.
sources.locator: Sections on measuring RH, monitoring buildings/rooms and cases; indexed lines 300–315; also lines 337–342 on evidence before control changes.
sources.observed_operation: Guidance explains RH locality/time dependence, favors recording instruments near collections, advises multiple locations where conditions differ, and says a full year may be needed to see seasonal case behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Monitoring period and positions depend on whether question is local temperature/RH variability or seasonal transmission; page warns against changing historic climate control without evidence.
sources.applicability: Supports the proposed observation-first environmental alternative and causal caution; does not supply room data or authorize an RH setpoint for this case.
sources.evidence_used: 12-month monitor proposal, local logger placement and caution against inferring cause from anecdotal damage.

sources.title: Caring for paper objects — Preventive conservation guidelines for collections
sources.creators: Canadian Conservation Institute, Government of Canada
sources.version_or_release: Undated current online guidance; no edition/version date displayed on the accessed page.
sources.locator: § Incorrect relative humidity, indexed lines 500–540; especially dimensional changes and restraint lines 500–521 and monitoring/enclosure recommendations lines 531–540.
sources.observed_operation: Guidance describes paper moisture absorption/desorption and dimensional change, differential response of joined materials and constraints, plus measuring instruments and enclosure practices.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Guidance conditions recommendations on paper-object sensitivity and assembly; it distinguishes single sheets from restrained or layered objects.
sources.applicability: Conservation context for the collected paper labels/annotations and possible enclosures; does not test labels adhered to synthetic sleeves or diagnose this store.
sources.evidence_used: Independent dimensional endpoint and restraint/interactions rationale.

sources.title: Modified Acrylate Pressure-Sensitive Adhesives for Low-Surface-Energy Substrate and Adhesion Mechanism Models
sources.creators: Primary study indexed by NCBI PubMed; DOI 10.3390/polym17091130
sources.locator: Abstract and conflict-of-interest statement; PubMed lines 227–251 in opened record.
sources.observed_operation: Abstract reports modified acrylate PSA tests on HDPE, including 24-hour peel/tack at 20°C, and reduced peel strength as temperature rose; one author was employed by the collaborating adhesive company.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Specific experimental adhesive and HDPE model; reported result does not generalize to untreated/treatment-unknown PE/PP sleeves, other adhesives, long-term storage or conservation safety.
sources.applicability: Conditional lead if sleeve polymer and adhesive identity support it; use to justify substrate/product identification, not to select a product.
sources.evidence_used: Low-surface-energy interface hypothesis and explicit generalizability/conflict limitation.

sources.title: Labeling Natural History Collections
sources.creators: Erika Range, Luci Cipera and Carolyn Leckie; Society for the Preservation of Natural History Collections
sources.locator: Sections 4.3 Adhesive Attachment, 4.4 Outstanding Materials Questions, Decision Making and Future Research; indexed lines 269–296 and 313–330.
sources.observed_operation: Professional field review distinguishes attachment modes and summarizes competing label material standards; it records questions and testing gaps, including plastic substrates, adhesive aging, and print adhesion.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Natural-history collection context; guidance and a literature/standards synthesis, not primary comparative data or controlling requirements for this invented volunteer-store case.
sources.applicability: Useful map of unfamiliar label/attachment approaches and unresolved evidence; avoid relying on its summaries as primary authority.
sources.evidence_used: Component decomposition, unknowns and an explicit reason to require supplier specs and local testing.

sources.title: Object labelling
sources.version_or_release: Current institutional training page; publication/update date not displayed; ©2026.
sources.locator: Sections Adding a label and When not to label; indexed lines 68–95 and 114–120.
sources.observed_operation: Guidance asks for secure, reversible, safe, visible identification and suggests a simple Tyvek tag for a fragile or loan object.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Institutional guidance for object labelling; tag use is a context-specific option and not a validated design for this store's sleeve.
sources.applicability: Analog for a nonadhesive mock-up that avoids contact with the collection object; test snagging, visibility and retrieval locally.
sources.evidence_used: Alternative approach only; no product endorsement.
